newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanians told to revive spirit of protest.
newsitem.headline: Albanians told to revive spirit of protest.

text.p: The leader of a student revolt that toppled communism in Albania six years ago called on workers and students on Friday to revive a spirit of protest to improve their rights under democracy.

Azem Hajdari, a hero of the December 1990 revolution who fell out with the ruling Democratic Party he helped found, staged a rally in Tirana to call for the resignation of the head of state-run television.

Hajdari accused TV chief Qemal Sakajeva of sanctioning biased reporting and of broadcasting programmes telling Albanians they had never had it so good when in reality many people were suffering economic hardship.

A crowd of around 200 people turned out to take part in the protest near the television headquarters. Hajdari said Tirana authorities blocked streets near the university campus to prevent students attending.
Protestors carried banners, reading "Down with corruption", "We want higher pensions and wages" and "We want television to be independent".
"I call on all trade unions to unite and demand better economic treatment and I call on students to unite with them to ask better living conditions and to fight corruption and crime," Hajdari said.
Hajdari says he was elected leader of the Independent Trade Unions, Albania's biggest union body, by a union congress but a court ruled he could not take up the post.
He warned political parties that they could not exist if they did not support the trade unions and called on the government to double wages to help the poorest in society.
Koha Jone daily quoted Hajdari on Friday as telling students he had to speak out to remind young people in Albania of the ideals they fought for in 1990.
Veteran trade unionist Luftim Ahmetaj told Hajdari at the Tirana protest that he should lead the union fight for better pay and conditions.
